subject: Mythology
title: The Seven Lucky Gods
description: A fast breakdown of The Seven Lucky Gods for builders.

hook.text: Seven gods sail together on a treasure ship every New Year, bringing luck, wealth, and happiness to Japan.

buildup.text: They come from three different religions: Shinto, Buddhism, and Taoism — blended into one joyful crew.

discovery.text: Ebisu brings business luck, Daikokuten brings wealth, and Benzaiten brings music and artistic talent.

twist.text: Only one of the seven is originally Japanese — Ebisu. The others were borrowed from China and India.

climax.text: Placing a picture of their treasure ship under your pillow on New Year's Eve is said to bring lucky dreams.

punchline.text: Japan built its luckiest tradition by borrowing gods from every neighbor.

quiz.question: What is unique about the Seven Lucky Gods of Japan?
options: They are all female deities from ancient Shinto
Only one is originally Japanese; the rest come from Chinese and Indian traditions
They each represent a different season of the year
